text: The burden of the wilderness the Sea: Like whirlwinds in the Negev passing through, it comes from the wilderness, from a fearsome land.
A harsh vision is declared to me: “The treacherous one deals treacherously, and the destroyer destroys. Go up, O Elam! Besiege, O Media! All her sighing I have made cease.”
Upon thus my loins are filled [with] pain; pangs have taken hold of me like the pangs of one giving birth. I am writhing from hearing; I am disturbed from seeing.
My heart staggers, a shuddering terrifies me; the twilight of my desire has been set for me into fear,
to arrange the table [and] lay out the spread, to eat, to drink. Rise up, O princes, [and] anoint the shield!
For thus the Lord has said to me: “Go, station the one keeping watch and let him declare what he sees.
And he sees a chariot [with] a pair of horses, the rider of a donkey, [and] the rider of a camel, and he will be attentive, [with] great attention.”
And the lookout called out: “Upon the watchtower, my Lord, I stand continually by day, and at my post I take [my] stand every night.
And behold this, the chariot of a man is coming, [with] a pair of horses.” And he answered and said, “Fallen, Babylon has fallen! And all the images of her gods He has broken to the ground!”
O my threshing, and the son of my threshing floor, that which I have heard from YHWH of Hosts, the God of Israel, I have declared to you⁺!
The burden of Dumah: To me one is calling from Seir: “Watchman, what of the night? Watchman, what of the night?”
The watchman said, “The morning comes, and also the night. If you⁺ would inquire, [then] inquire; return, come.”
The burden upon Arabia: In the thicket you⁺ lodge in Arabia, O caravans of Dedanites,
to meet the thirsty one. Bring water, O dwellers of the land of Tema, with his bread meet the one fleeing.
For they do flee from the face of swords, from the sword drawn, and from the bow bent, and from the weight of war.
For thus says the Lord to me: “Within a year, according to the years of a hireling, then will end all the glory of Kedar.
And the remnant of the number of archers, the mighty ones of the sons of Kedar, will be few.” For YHWH, the God of Israel, has spoken.
